note: The public, versioned capability-tag registry for the operator-blind background-task mechanism (ADR 0021). A capability tag is the OPAQUE token that rides the job envelope and the worker's claim on the wire and in the DB, so a bare database dump sees `02f271ff`, not `grant-delivery`. Each tag value is the first 4 bytes (8 lowercase hex chars) of SHA-256 over `veyq/v1/task-capability/<name>` — deterministic, no central assignment authority, extensible. This keeps gratuitous plaintext semantic labels out of the store (defence vs. a bare dump); it does NOT hide the kind of work from a correlating operator (that residual leak is correlation-bounded, documented in ADR 0021 and docs/crosscutting/background-tasks.md). Both surfaces (backend Kotlin, web TS) pin these exact values; a conformance test asserts the shipped constant equals the registry, the same drift-proofing the crypto vectors get.

grant-delivery.description: Deliver a scope grant to a pending (grant-less) member: any online key-holder wraps K_SC to the target member's identity public key (asymWrap to a foreign identity, context `scope-grant`) and posts the ciphertext as that member's wrappedGrant. Universal tag, no lease needed (idempotent, first-online-wins). The first, trivially-blind consumer of the mechanism (ADR 0020).

scope-rotation.description: Complete a queued group-key rotation after a co-shared member was cut with no key-holder online to rotate synchronously (en.spaces.scope-key-rotation §E1, ADR 0025 — groups rotate). Originated by the server on a tenant-member removal that cut a shared GROUP membership (the removing owner is not necessarily a key-holder there, so cannot mint the new epoch). Unlike grant-delivery this is NOT reconcilable from DB state: a removal cut advances no epoch and leaves no stale-epoch mismatch, so the pending-rotation state is recorded explicitly as this job (resourceRef == scopeId). The next online remaining key-holder claims it, mints E_{n+1} + wraps E_n + re-grants the surviving member set on-device (reusing the cr-0089 rotation-commit POST /api/scopes/{scopeId}/epochs), then completes. One live job per scope coalesces multiple removals (a single rotation re-grants exactly the current members); idempotent + first-online-wins. Operator-blind: opaque tag + scopeId + the resulting ciphertext epoch-link/re-grants — the server never mints, wraps, or holds a key.
